paragraphs.text: Power-Up — small, opt-in upgrades for DeepSeek Harness.
# Power-Up

Small, opt-in upgrades for DeepSeek Harness.
The upgrades include a **right-click action menu in the

Trajectory view**, a
**copyable step reference** that an agent can resolve back into the raw sessio

n
data, an optional **stop reason for background jobs**, an in-place
**plugin installer**, and a **s

idebar launcher** that turns the left sidebar's
panel list into an adaptive icon grid with drag sort

ing, folders, a
back-to-conversation tile, and restart/close tiles.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then open a session, switch to **Trajectory**, and right-click a record row.
## What it does
Right-click a trajectory record:

- **Copy content** — copy the full text of the record.
- **Copy as quote** — produce a Markdown bloc

kquote with the record kind.
- **Quote in composer** — insert that quote into the current input box.

- **Open record details** — open the host's record inspector.
- **Fork from here** — fork the sessi

on at that record (inclusive).
- **Copy step reference** — copy `dsh-step:<session-id>/<step-id>`; t

he
`powerup_step_read` tool turns that string back into the raw session data.
- **Copy session ID**.
Right-click empty space in the ledger:

- **Export trajectory JSON** — save the current trajectory snapshot.
- **Copy session ID**.
- **Open
the Power-Up page** — the sidebar control panel.

The sidebar **Power-Up** page turns the menu on or off and lists the available
actions. The setting

is stored in the browser. It also holds the defaults for
**one-click install** (auto-enable and auto

-restart), which the plugin installer
uses.
### Stop a background job with a reason

The session header's background jobs panel keeps the host's list, live output,
and stop button. Clic

king a running job's stop button opens a themed Power-Up
dialog instead of the host's two-press stop

. The dialog is portaled to the
document body, so it renders above the jobs menu (which is itself a

body portal)
and is not clipped by any slot's stacking context; its colors come only from
`--dsw-ali
as-*` tokens, so light and dark themes both work.

- The reason field is optional; an empty field keeps the host's default
`cancelled by the user` reas

on. `Enter` confirms while `Esc` cancels.
- Confirming stops the job through the Host route, which r

ecords
`cancelled by the user: <reason>`. The completion notice injected into the
session and the sh

ell tool's result therefore carry the reason.
- If the button cannot be resolved to a live job, the

click is left alone and
the host's original stop flow runs unchanged.
### Menu keys
`↑` / `↓` move, `Home` / `End` jump, `Enter` runs, `Esc` closes.
### Step references

**Copy step reference** copies a single line such as
`dsh-step:session-1a2b…/turn.0.step.3`. The ref

erence carries the session id
plus a stable step id:
| Step id | Copied from | Resolves to |
| `turn.<turn>.step.<step>` | an assistant row | every raw event between `step/start` and `step/end`

|
| `call.<call-id>` | a tool row | that tool call and its `tool/result` |
| `seq.<n>` | any other

raw-event row | that single event |
| `index.<n>` | a synthetic row | nothing — the menu disables th

row | that single event |
| `index.<n>` | a synthetic row | nothing — the menu disables the action |

Paste the line into the session and the agent can call
**`powerup_step_read`**, a read-only Host too

l registered while both `tools` and
`sessionQuery` are composed:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

It returns the raw events as JSON. Optional arguments: `before` / `after` add up
to 50 neighboring e

vents on each side, and `requests: true` also includes the
`request/header` snapshots (the full syst

em prompt and tool schemas), which are
omitted by default because they are large. The tool is worksp

ace-agnostic: it
reads the session named in the reference through `ctx.sessionQuery`, so an agent
ca
n open a step in a session it never had to locate on disk.
### Sidebar launcher

The left sidebar's global panel buttons (Conversation, Files, Plugins, and the
entries other plugins
add) become an icon grid instead of a one-per-row list:

- **Columns follow the width.** The list is an `auto-fill` grid of
`minmax(58px, 1fr)` cells, so wid

ening the sidebar adds columns and narrowing
it removes them — there is no fixed column count to bre

ak.
- **Icons above labels.** Each tile stacks a 20px icon over an 11px caption, one
line with an el

lipsis when the label is long.
- **Drag to sort.** Press and drag a tile; a ghost follows the pointe

r and a
thin accent line marks the insertion point. Order is stored per browser.
- **Drop onto a til

e's middle to build a folder.** Dropping on the middle of
another icon folds both into a folder tile

(like a Windows Start menu folder);
dropping on a folder adds to it; dropping a folder onto an icon

or another
folder merges them. Click a folder and the contained icons appear in a flyout
anchored t

o the tile, scaling in from its edge. Inside the flyout: click an
entry to open that panel, `×` remo

ves it from the folder, click the title to
rename the folder, and **Ungroup** returns every member t

o the grid.
- **The host's "More" entry is a tile too.** The host wraps its extra-panels
menu in a `

Menu` root `<span>` around the row button (not a div), so the
launcher resolves any non-button child

that owns a direct button as that
entry; it gets the same stacked icon/label tile and can be dragge

d like any
other panel, including into a folder.
- **A synthetic "Back to conversation" tile.** Powe

r-Up adds one extra tile of
its own (chat glyph + label) that calls `layout.selectPanel(null)` to re

turn
to the Conversation; it highlights when no global panel is selected and can be
placed anywhere

by dragging, including into a folder.
- **A synthetic "Restart DSH" tile.** A second Power-Up tile (

a ring with the
arrowhead tangent to the top, i.e. the arrow lines up with the arc) plus
`重启` / `Res

tart` opens the same restart confirmation the pending-restart
bar uses: the tile only calls into tha

t React prompt, so there is one dialog,
[该节后续省略]
## Install a plugin

Open the built-in **Plugins** page. Every third-party card under **Installed
plugins** gains a small

install icon in its action area. Clicking it opens the
install dialog:

registries — the sam

e list the **Add plugin** dialog offers, including the
